ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the rolling mill workshop of a steel plant, there is a cold rolling machine for steel plates as shown in the figure. The thicker steel plate is rolled into a thinner steel plate at a constant speed by the rollers, and then neatly coiled into a steel plate roll. After a time $T$, the radius of the steel plate roll increases from $r$ to $2r$.

1. Find the time required for the radius to increase from $2r$ to $3r$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the rolling mill workshop of a steel plant, there is a cold rolling machine for steel plates as shown in the figure. The thicker steel plate is rolled into a thinner steel plate at a constant speed by the rollers, and then neatly coiled into a steel plate roll. After a time $T$, the radius of the steel plate roll increases from $r$ to $2r$. Find the time required for the radius to increase from $2r$ to $3r$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, on the left there is a relatively thick steel plate labeled “Heavy steel plate” entering between upper and lower rollers labeled “Rollers”; after passing through the rollers, a thin steel plate labeled “Thin steel sheet” is output on the right, and continues to be rolled into the steel coil labeled “Thin steel coil” on the right. Reasoning: The thin steel plate is continuously rolled into the steel coil at the constant speed stated in the problem, so the length of thin steel plate rolled in per unit time is constant. The thickness and width of the thin steel plate can be regarded as constant, so the amount of steel plate rolled into the steel coil is proportional to the annular area increased in the cross section of the steel coil. When the radius increases from r to 2r, the increased area is π[(2r)^2-r^2]=3πr^2, and the corresponding time is T. When the radius increases from 2r to 3r, the increased area is π[(3r)^2-(2r)^2]=5πr^2. Time is proportional to area, so the required time is (5πr^2)/(3πr^2)·T=5T/3.
